release_scope: Bounded installed-PWA update-lifecycle successor of exact v101.153 R1. Repairs B24H-003 proven by physical v101.148→v101.153 update evidence: the old 5-second controller-transition timeout began before registration.update(), so shell download/install time could exhaust the window and force close/reopen. v101.154 observes controllerchange before update but starts a 30-second transition wait only after update() returns, and precaches one canonical HTML shell instead of three byte-identical navigation aliases. Corpus/devotional text, Search, scroll/resume, highlighting, personal-state schemas and transaction semantics remain unchanged.
real_device_status: Physical evidence on the predecessor line: installed PWA running v101.148 detected v101.153 but could not complete the in-app controller transition; closing and reopening activated v101.153. This is recorded as B24H-003 / seamless installed-update FAIL for v101.153. v101.154 has deterministic internal negative/positive lifecycle evidence; physical installed-PWA update to v101.154 remains NOT_TESTED.
postfreeze_reopen_evidence: B24H-003 physical predecessor evidence: v101.148→v101.153 in-app update did not transition the running installed PWA; close/reopen loaded v101.153. Exact v148 and v153 packages use byte-identical update functions, proving the weakness was inherited. v101.154 repairs only update lifecycle timing/cache-shell duplication plus release bindings.
blind_adversarial_finding: B24H-001: predecessor manifest.json declared v101.145 while active page/SW/version identity was v101.146 R1.
four_pass_finding: B24H-002: at exactly 768 CSS px, the 768–1149 tablet rule hid .bottom-nav while the legacy sidebar/menu were globally disabled; 767px and 769px retained navigation.
pwa_update_physical_finding: B24H-003: running installed PWA v101.148 could not complete seamless update to v101.153; closing/reopening was required. Root cause: controllerchange timeout started before registration.update()/shell install and expired after 5 seconds; required-shell install also fetched three aliases of the same ~2.6 MB HTML.
